title: 18.7 billion tokens, 1,181 commits,  6 months (so far): the real numbers behind building my Godot management sim with Claude Code
author: bahaw1024
selftext:
I had my daughter draw/write the logo and used AI to extract each letter and put it in my artwork. She writes her S/Z's backwards lol   
  
I've spent the last 6 months building **Hookah House**, a cozy hookah lounge management sim (seat guests -> take orders -> prep bowls -> run coals -> get paid -> expand your lounge), with Claude Code as my main development partner. The Steam page went live in April. Since this sub is about workflow, not just results, here are the actual numbers off my machine.

**The receipts (Feb 27 → Aug 31):**

* 1,181 commits
* \~205,000 lines of GDScript across 1,084 files
* 1,877 unit tests, run headless on every change
* 132 Claude Code sessions
* 77 million tokens of output actually written by the model
* 18.7 billion total tokens processed (the gap is prompt-cache reads; context is the real cost)

**Stack:**

* **Engine:** Godot 4.4 (GDScript, Forward+)
* **Dev agent:** Claude Code, with project rules in CLAUDE.md, persistent memory files for engine gotchas, and custom subagents (compile/test verifier, visual probe, web-export guard, save-migration auditor)
* **3D assets:** Meshy + Tripo (text/image → 3D), Mixamo animations retargeted onto one shared rig, cleanup in Blender
* **Audio:** ElevenLabs SFX, LUFS-normalized onto audio buses
* **Backend:** one Cloudflare Worker (live player count)
* **CI:** GitHub Actions running the same headless compile + test suite as local

**What actually worked:**

* **Making the agent verify itself.** A stop hook compiles all \~800 game scripts (\~9s) and runs the full 1,877-test suite (\~12s) any time it touches a script. It cannot end a turn on broken code. This single thing did more for quality than any prompt engineering.
* **Persistent memory.** Every engine trap it hits (headless false-passes, navmesh carving stranding the player, glTF export scene leaks) gets written to a memory file, so it never re-learns the same lesson twice. After 6 months this is basically a private "Godot gotchas" wiki it wrote for itself.
* **Data-driven everything.** Furniture, flavors, and decor all live in JSON catalogs, so new content is data, not code, and the agent adds items without touching systems.
* **Simulation over vibes for balance.** A headless sim runs full game-days and diffs against "feel bands" before any balance number is allowed to change.

**What burned me:**

* **Generative 3D has no free retries.** A generation that comes back visually broken still reports SUCCEEDED and bills in full. Every asset now keeps its prompt + reference image in the repo so a redo is a decision, not a reflex.
* **Headless engine testing lies.** Crashed coroutines can still print "ALL PASSED", transforms don't propagate, and skinned poses need bone-level number checks. A real chunk of my tooling exists purely to catch false greens.
* **The agent will cheerfully spend your money.** Hard rule #1 in my project instructions is now "never spend credits without per-call permission." Ask me how I learned that.

The game, if you want to see what all those tokens bought: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4607750/Hookah\_House/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4607750/Hookah_House/) (wishlists genuinely help a solo dev). Website: [https://hookahhousegame.com](https://hookahhousegame.com)

Happy to go deep on any part of the workflow: the hooks, subagents, memory setup, the asset pipeline, or costs.

comments.author: Pixel_Lover
comments.body: Hey, it looks good and i gotta say i admire the workflow you described. Is there any chance you share the specific tree-structure of the project and some of the Gotcha prompts? Especially for the 3D generation since it is very expensive... I am trying to build a sim aswell but way simpler (at least in the begining) and i've just started working on some Godot tutorials. In any case good job! Wishlisted :)

comments.author: AlgaeNo3373
comments.body:
I say this with love. Genuinely I just want to help here not bark people down. I think that texture glitch in your Steam page's trailer is kinda killing you. 

https://i.redd.it/wqsv6fqm5wmh1.gif

It'd seem pedantic maybe, but you just got through having your LLM tell me about how sprawling and huge this thing is. This is the kinda one hour fix (and a priority one at that if it's part of marketing material) I expect to be mercilessly hunted and eradicated in the process of *six months* and *billions* of tokens (jfc bro). Maybe that's what spurred my reaction here, IDK. But dude. If you saw *that*, after all *that months of work and tokens*, and thought "eh, good enough for Steam" then I have to wonder about what *else* has slipped past the apparently undiscerning eye?

Or in other words: "A generation that comes back visually broken still reports SUCCEEDED and bills in full."
